name: Game & Watch
description: Nintendo's line of single-game LCD handhelds, launched in 1980 and sold until 1991. Each unit plays one game on a pre-printed segment LCD and doubles as a clock and alarm. The line established Nintendo in portable gaming and set up the Game Boy that followed.

specs.graphics: Segmented LCD with fixed, pre-printed graphics
specs.media: None, one built-in game per unit

curiosities: Gunpei Yokoi reportedly got the idea after watching a bored commuter play with an LCD calculator on a bullet train.
The Donkey Kong Game & Watch (1982) introduced the cross-shaped directional pad that Nintendo later patented and put on the NES controller.
Several models, such as Donkey Kong and Oil Panic, used a clamshell with two screens, the format the Nintendo DS later revived.
Nintendo released new Game & Watch units for Super Mario Bros. in 2020 and The Legend of Zelda in 2021 as anniversary products.
story: Gunpei Yokoi had the idea after seeing a man playing with a calculator on a train. Nintendo's Game & Watch, launched in 1980, was a single game with a clock on an LCD screen.
Ball, Fire, Octopus and the dual-screen Donkey Kong of 1982, where the D-pad was introduced, sold more than 40 million units in all.
Its D-pad became the standard for controllers, and its dual screens returned on the Nintendo DS.
